key_points: Ronald Reagan, known as the 'Great Communicator,' rose from radio announcer and Hollywood actor to California governor before becoming the oldest elected U.S. president at the time, at age 69 in 1980.

As president, Reagan focused on reducing federal government influence and cutting taxes, which coincided with falling unemployment and economic growth, though critics say it widened the gap between rich and middle-class Americans and sharply increased the national debt.
Reagan built up U.S. military spending as part of his strategy to pressure the Soviet Union, and by the end of his term the Berlin Wall came down, which many credit partly to his policies.
Reagan survived an assassination attempt and the Iran-Contra scandal, involving secretly selling weapons to Iran, without losing significant public support, leaving office with majority approval.
main_idea: Ronald Reagan, known as a skilled communicator, pursued conservative economic policies and a tougher stance toward the Soviet Union as president, and despite controversies like Iran-Contra, he left office with strong public support.
restate_sentence: As president, Reagan is credited for changing the direction of the country.
